terms.grammar: pronoun: the ordinary forms of vōs, used reflexively
evidence: Cic. Agr. 2.29.79: dēlūdī vōsmet ipsōs … patiēminī? (Lewis & Short, s.v. dēlūdō)
terms.comment: No separate reflexive; stressed, vōsmet or vōsmet ipsōs. English “enjoy yourselves” and “look after yourselves” need no reflexive in Latin: ut vōbīs suāviter sit; date operam ut valeātis.

evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 104: ut ea contrā vōsmet ipsōs facere videāminī (Lewis & Short, s.v. contrā)
terms.comment: Agrees with vōs as subject or as object, as with yourself.

phrases.latin: dēlūdī vōsmet ipsōs diūtius ā tribūnō plēbis patiēminī?
phrases.english: Will you let yourselves be fooled any longer by a tribune of the people?

phrases.latin: ut ea contrā vōsmet ipsōs facere videāminī
phrases.english: so that you seem to be doing it against yourselves

phrases.latin: vōs rogō, amīcī, ut vōbīs suāviter sit
phrases.english: I ask you, friends, to enjoy yourselves.

phrases.latin: maximē autem date operam ut valeātis, sī nōs vultis valēre
phrases.english: Above all, take good care of yourselves, if you want me to be well.

sources: Lewis & Short: vos · Lewis & Short: ipse

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
